title: Implement a Multi-Tiered Rate Limiting Feature
description: The SocialPulse Gateway is experiencing a surge in traffic, including some automated abuse. To ensure stability and fair usage, a new rate-limiting feature is required. This task involves designing, implementing, and testing a configurable, multi-tiered rate-limiting system. The implementation will span multiple development sessions, starting with architectural analysis and design, followed by core implementation, and finally integration and testing. The agent must retain context between sessions to build upon its previous work.

project_spec.name: SocialPulse Gateway
project_spec.description:
SocialPulse Gateway is an expert-level, TypeScript-based API gateway designed for large-scale social platforms that aggregate diverse interaction streams—posts, reactions, live chats, and stories—into a single, coherent programmable surface. Sitting in front of a constellation of micro-services (timeline, media, messaging, notifications, and social-graph), it exposes both REST and GraphQL entry points while enforcing strict clean_architecture boundaries: presentation (controllers/resolvers), application (use-cases & DTOs), domain (aggregates, value objects, policies), and infrastructure (adapters & external integrations).

The gateway prioritizes social-centric concerns such as activity-feed fan-out, real-time presence, and community safety. Built-in rate-limiting and behavioral analytics guard against abusive patterns like follow-spam or message floods. Versioned routing enables gradual rollout of social algorithms (e.g., ranking V2) without breaking third-party clients. Response caching (Redis) accelerates high-fanout endpoints—public timelines, trending hashtags—while WebSocket subscriptions for GraphQL keep users up-to-date with new likes or comments. Comprehensive monitoring, structured logging, and OpenAPI/GraphQL self-documentation make the gateway production-ready for a rapidly evolving social ecosystem.
dependencies: ajv (JSON Schema validation for dynamic message payloads)
typedi or tsyringe (dependency injection for clean_architecture)
type-graphql (code-first schema tied to application layer)
